newsitem.title: UK: N. Sea grades firmer again, Dated premiums lower.
newsitem.headline: N. Sea grades firmer again, Dated premiums lower.

text.p: North Sea grade differentials took another step higher on Friday after trading at progressively higher numbers this week.
Forties and Statfjord for around Oct 22 both traded five cents up from previous deals at Dated Brent plus 35 cents.
Dealers said only seven cargoes, other than Brent, remained available up to October 20 after refiners bought heavily earlier in the week.
Just one Statfjord, one Forties and a number of Ekofisks remained, said one North Sea producer.
Sellers for later October cargoes asked higher numbers but refiners stood back on Friday, waiting to see which way refinery margins would move, before they pitched in to the market again.
But Dated Brent was unable to repeat the higher sales of Thursday of Nov +7 and +12 cents, trading on Friday at +6 cents on Friday for an Oct 6-8 cargo.
Twelve cargoes, nine held by two companies were left available after four cargoes were nominated loading dates on Friday. One of the four was five o'clocked.
Intermonth paper Brent spreads were unmoved in a virtually untraded market, valuing Oct/Nov at about +40 cents and Nov/Dec at +50 cents.
Urals in the Mediterranean was steady at about Dated Brent -65/70 cents cif.
But gas oil's rise this week helped maintain Syrian Light after trades at OSP +10 cents.
The Dubai market took the tender award by Indian Oil Corp of four cargoes for November in its stride, leaving intermonth and Brent/Dubai spreads steady.
